text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Despite growing competition on Poland's soft drinks market Pepsi Cola-General Bottlers will increase production by 30 percent in 1997, company president Bob Shaffer said.

- A German shipping company offered to start a car-ferry connection in the bay of Szczecin, northwestern Poland, between Nowe Warpno and Altwarp, Szczecin representative Magdalena Wysznacka-Zurawska said.
- A new soft commodities exchange will be set up in Bronisze-Ozarow, Warsaw province, in two years time, the commodity exchange managing company's (RSRH) president Jacek Kalinski said.
- Holland's DAF truck maker has set up its DAF Truck Poland branch office to carry out the marketing of the firm's Dutch-made trucks and the sales of vehicles to be made in Poland in the future.
- The state-owned railway company PKP has ordered fifty new generation ABB Henschel electric engines worth $200 million from the Wroclaw-based Pafawag rolling stock maker.
The contract will allow Germany's Adtranz to become a strategic investor in the plant.

- The sales of the Poznan-based Hipolit Cegielski (HCP) ship-engine maker will reach 440 million zlotys, which represents a 45.5 percent increase compared with last year's results, HCP president Waclaw Piotrowski said.

- Trade unions in the CPN petrol distribution chain have taken legal action to guarantee employment and social security for workers, as well as changes in the government's petrochemical industry restructuring programme.
- The Gdynia-based Bank Komunalny bank will conduct a municipal bond issue for the municipality of Pieniezno in northern Poland.
- The Bialystok-based Pakpol packaging maker invested $7.5 million in facility development last year.
Its revenues were 31.22 million zlotys while net profit was at 850,000 zlotys, the company said.
NOWA EUROPA

- Poland's largest insurance firm PZU operates against the law now as it lacks 400 million zlotys to fulfil financial regulations imposed by the state insurance supervision office (PUNU), PUNU president Danuta Walcerz said.

- The Lublin-branch of Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), Poland's telecom monopolist, employed monopolistic practices through leasing contracts which eliminated other firms from the market, a ruling by Poland's Anti-monopoly Court said.
- The Wielun-based ZUGIL galvanised coatings maker will construct roofing for the football stadium to be built in Paris before the world soccer championships in 1998.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The International Monetary Fund (IMF) supports Poland's current economic strategy agreed by the government and the National bank of Poland, the central bank, IMF representative Markus Rodlauer said.

- Subsidies in the European Union's PHARE programme for border area development at the Polish-Czech-German border will reach 1.5 million European Currency Units (ECU) by 1999, an agreement signed in Warsaw on Wednesday said.
ZYCIE
Poland's annual milk consumption per capita has fallen by 70 litres since 1987 and is now at 200 litres, a report by the food and nutrition research institute said.
PARKIET

- Poland's gross domestic product (GDP) in 1996 will be 357 billion zlotys, its growth in real terms decreasing by 1.5 percent compared with last year's results, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
The decline was caused by a slowdown in the industrial output and construction sector, GUS said.
- In the first ten months of 1996 the listed Zywiec brewery's net profit was 76 percent lower than in the same period last year despite growing revenues.
